subject: Follow-up: Residency & region routing impacts for deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmemedtech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Residency & region routing impacts for deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sarah / Tomás — thanks again for the intro call earlier today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have everything captured.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary constraint: EU data residency for PHI-adjacent telemetry — legal wants processing and storage within EU borders where possible.
- Secondary constraint: APAC offices need acceptable latency for inference; team will accept a slightly higher latency if we can ensure EU-only processing for primary patient datasets.
- Use case: real-time triage (low-latency text generation) + nightly bulk embeddings for analytics.
- Procurement: target decision window Q2; legal/infosec will kick off SOC2 and KMS questions.

Rails we discussed (short):
- Hosted API (EU region): fastest path, self-serve, regional endpoints. Good for quick POC but need clarity on cross-region fallback policies.
- Dedicated capacity (EU-only, reserved GPUs): provides predictable throughput and isolation, can be configured to avoid cross-region fallback for most scenarios.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): required if legal insists on customer-controlled networking + HSM-managed keys and zero cross-border egress.

Open items / asks from your side:
1) Confirm whether legal requires strict EU-only egress for ALL workloads vs only for PHI-related data.
2) Share a simple network/dataflow diagram (we discussed a PNG you mentioned).
3) Provide a rough procurement timeline and procurement contact.

Proposed next steps (my suggestions):
- Technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer to map network flows and produce a gated deployment recommendation (30–45m). Laura, can you run this?
- I will send our deployment options deck + SOC2 questionnaire for legal review.
- Tentative SE deep-dive window: Thu 2026-03-11 09:00 CET / 00:00 PDT — does that work for you?

Attachments I will send: redwood-deployment-options-slide.pdf, SOC2-questionnaire.pdf.

Thanks — I’ll hold a tentative slot once I hear back on availability.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmemedtech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@acmemedtech.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Residency & region routing impacts for deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from legal/infra before we lock the SE session: 

1) EU-only egress: legal has said "EU-only for patient data at rest and in-transit" — however they are asking whether that can be enforced at the platform level (i.e., no cross-border routing even in failover). If Hosted must replicate logs or telemetry to non-EU for observability, that will be a blocker.

2) Key management: we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption of patient datasets. Can Redwood integrate with our Azure Key Vault or do we need a Private deployment for HSM?

3) Latency: our APAC team is small but needs sub-200ms median for routing to triage flows. If we keep inference in EU, what's the expected APAC latency and are there caching strategies to keep experience acceptable?

I've attached a rough dataflow diagram (acme-dataflow-overview.png) that shows which datasets must remain in EU. Procurement timeline: aiming for contract signature by end of Q2. Procurement contact: maria.perez@acmemedtech.com.

If you can have Laura or someone on infra outline the specific technical limits for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private around cross-region egress, that would help speed the legal review.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Infrastructure, AcmeMedTech

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmemedtech.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Residency & region routing impacts for deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sarah — Laura from Solutions Engineering. Thanks for the diagram, that helps. High-level technical answers below, plus a proposed SE deep-dive agenda.

Platform capabilities (short):
- Hosted API (regional endpoints): We offer regional Hosted endpoints (eu-west-1, eu-central-1, etc.). For normal operation, data is processed and cached within the requested region. However, cross-region routing can occur in platform-level failover scenarios (extreme outages) unless you opt into Dedicated or Private where fallbacks are configurable.
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools pinned to a region. By design we can configure policies to prefer no cross-region fallback for inference requests; some control-plane metadata (non-sensitive telemetry) may still be routed for observability unless we enable longer-term enterprise controls. We can provide an EU-only Dedicated deployment with contractual egress constraints.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full customer-controlled networking. No cross-border egress unless you explicitly allow it. Supports Azure Key Vault and HSM integrations (bring-your-own-key) and on-prem HSM if needed.

KMS/HSM integration:
- Hosted: supports envelope keys; for strict customer-managed keys we recommend Dedicated with a KMS bridge or Private with direct KMS/HSM integration.

Latency & caching:
- Approx latencies (round-trip, best-effort numbers): EU-hosted to EU client ~30–80ms median; APAC clients to EU-hosted ~180–350ms depending on network path.
- Caching strategies: prefix/KV caches and edge caching for embeddings can significantly reduce perceived latency for repeated requests. We can pre-warm caches in an APAC-adjacent region if you choose Dedicated spares or multi-region setup.

Data egress guarantees:
- Hosted: we can commit to regional processing under normal ops, but cannot guarantee zero cross-region routing in catastrophic failovers without moving to Dedicated (with contractual controls) or Private.
- Dedicated: contractual commitments for EU-only processing, plus options to cut control-plane telemetry if required.
- Private: full control — no cross-border routing unless configured.

Proposed SE deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
1) Walkthrough of acme-dataflow-overview.png (5–10m)
2) Map each dataset to residency requirement and policy implications (10m)
3) Deployment recommendation (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) per workload, including cost/latency tradeoffs (10–15m)
4) KMS/HSM and procurement checklist (5–10m)

I attached our quick deployment options slide that summarizes differences at a glance. Please let me know which time works; I can do Thu 2026-03-11 09:00 CET as suggested. Also if you can share a small sample of typical request size and QPS for triage flows that will help size Dedicated pools and caching.

—
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-deployment-options-slide.pdf]
